title: Support documents nobody trusts
honesty_boundary: This tool is a scoping aid for checkable trial definitions, not a guarantee of outcomes. Synthetic demo claims describe fictional examples and no real engagements. Evidence pointers are supplied by the input and are not independently inspected.
problem: A support team wants a repeatable way to inspect a fixed set of help documents for broken links and missing required sections.

artifact.name: Support documentation audit bundle
artifact.format: A runnable standard-library checker and three CSV result files.
artifact.scope_limit: The artifact is limited to the mapped capabilities and listed acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria.condition: source-map.csv contains exactly 12 data rows, each with non-empty source_id, section_heading, citation_locator values.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Count source-map.csv rows and inspect the 3 required columns for blank cells.

acceptance_criteria.condition: link-results.csv contains exactly 12 data rows: 10 PASS and 2 FAIL status values.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Count data rows and compare the status column values with the required totals.

acceptance_criteria.condition: issues.csv contains exactly 4 data rows: 2 broken-link findings and 2 missing-section findings.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Count issues.csv rows and group finding_type values into the 2 required categories.

assumptions: The buyer supplies a frozen bundle of 12 UTF-8 help documents and a required-section list.
The trial checks local copies and does not crawl or change a live help centre.
exclusions: No rewrite or factual review of support content.
No live website monitoring or content-management integration.

fixed_price.pricing_rule: GBP 750 per day plus GBP 125 per acceptance criterion; day count follows the documented scope threshold.
